mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the federal funds rate over 3 consecutive months indicates the Federal Reserve is shifting from tightening to easing monetary policy, lowering discount rates and increasing equity valuation multiples, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day forward returns in > 60% of macro-easing windows, or 20-day returns are not statistically higher than the 5-day pre-easing period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the federal funds rate above 5.25% triggers a risk-off reaction in equity markets, compressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate higher borrowing costs and reduced corporate credit availability.
failure_condition: SPX achieves positive 60-day forward returns in > 70% of post-tightening windows, or 60-day returns are not significantly lower than the 5-day pre-tightening period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) exceeding 10,000 over 3 months signals a labor market softening, reducing equity risk premia and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day forward returns in > 60% of softening episodes, or 5-day returns are not significantly higher than the 5-day pre-softening period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) below 8,000 for 3 consecutive months indicates strengthening labor market conditions, reducing discount rates and boosting S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day forward returns in > 60% of strengthening episodes, or 20-day returns are not significantly higher than the 5-day pre-strengthening period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production index (INDPRO) exceeding 102.5 for 3 consecutive months signals a supply-side expansion, lowering input costs and improving S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX achieves negative 60-day forward returns in > 70% of supply-side expansion episodes, or 60-day returns are not significantly higher than the 5-day pre-expansion period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the S&P 500 index (GDPC1) over 3 consecutive months indicates weakening aggregate demand, compressing equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day forward returns in > 60% of demand-weakening episodes, or 20-day returns are not significantly lower than the 5-day pre-weakening period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the S&P 500 index (GDPC1) above 1400 for 3 consecutive months signals a strong demand environment, lifting equity valuations and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX achieves negative 60-day forward returns in > 70% of strong demand episodes, or 60-day returns are not significantly higher than the 5-day pre-strong-demand period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the S&P 500 index (GDPC1) over 3 consecutive months combined with a rise in the CPIAUCSL index (CPI inflation) above 2% indicates a demand-driven inflationary pressure, compressing forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls > 3 consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL rises > 2% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day forward returns in > 60% of inflationary episodes, or 20-day returns are not significantly lower than the 5-day pre-inflationary period (t-test p > 0.05).
